# Mêlée

> Party games for one screen and the whole room. One screen runs the game and
> shows a QR code; everyone else joins from whatever screen they have to hand.
> No install, no account, no app store.

One person opens a room and gets a four-character code. Everyone else joins by
scanning the QR code on that screen or by typing the code — a phone, a laptop,
anything with a browser. The room stays open for the evening; the screen running
it plays the audio and shows the score.

## Games

- **Blind test** — a clip plays, the first to name the track and the artist
  scores. Tracks come from charts, a decade, film composers, a Deezer playlist
  or a search.
- **Buzzer** — the race with no content at all. The host brings the charade, the
  quiz on paper or the lesson; the screen only settles who was first.
- **Quiz** — question banks bundled with the server, in French and English, by
  subject.
- **Reflex** — the screen changes colour and the first in wins. Going before
  it changes costs the round.

## Pages

Every page below is served in English under `/en` and in French under `/fr`,
as its own document with its own `lang`, title and description. `/` carries no
language: it negotiates from the browser's and redirects, which is what
`hreflang="x-default"` points at.

- [Home](https://melee.adrienlcp.com/en): open a room, or join one with a code.
- [Blind test](https://melee.adrienlcp.com/en/blindtest)
- [Buzzer](https://melee.adrienlcp.com/en/buzzer)
- [Quiz](https://melee.adrienlcp.com/en/quiz)
- [Reflex](https://melee.adrienlcp.com/en/reflex)
- [Credits](https://melee.adrienlcp.com/en/credits)
- [Legal notice and privacy](https://melee.adrienlcp.com/en/legal): who
  publishes the site, what it keeps and for how long, and the third parties.

## Notes

A room's own pages — `/host/<code>` and `/play/<code>` — are not content. A code
is one evening long and is shared by hand, so those paths resolve only while the
room is open and are excluded in `robots.txt`.
